name: Relative Peeling Is Equivalent to an Inward USO Extension
statement: Let $T\subseteq H$ be nonempty ample classes and prescribe a unique-sink orientation $D_T$ on $T$. Then $H$ corner-peels to $T$ if and only if $D_T$ extends to a USO of $H$ whose boundary edges point into $T$ and whose orientation on $H\setminus T$ is acyclic. If $T$ is dismantlable ample, this is equivalent to an acyclic USO of $H$ with inward boundary at $T$, and every prescribed acyclic USO of $T$ extends.
proof: Reverse a relative peeling and add each deleted corner back as a source. Its corner cube supplies the outgoing-cube condition, every old cube keeps its unique sink, and the new sources form an acyclic outside orientation with boundary directed into $T$. Conversely, repeatedly delete a source of the outside acyclic digraph. The inward boundary makes it a source of the remaining whole USO; the outgoing-cube condition makes it a corner, and the restricted representation map stays valid. Iteration deletes exactly $H\setminus T$. If the prescribed orientation of $T$ is acyclic, no directed cycle can cross the inward boundary.
